function: Excluded, no_learning: BS beamforming, RIS phase shifts, bandwidth and user selection are designed by successive linear programming (classical optimization), not by a learned model (p. 1, p. 7).
notes: Exclusion code no_learning (Step 1, check 3). p. 1 (abstract): "The MINLP is transformed into a tractable nonlinear program, approximated via linear problems using Taylor expansion and solved with an iterative algorithm based on successive linear programming (SLP)." Section III.A (p. 7) and Algorithm 2 (p. 9) give the SLP with trust region that solves for W, Psi, f, b, alpha; there is no neural network, no training and no learned parameter in the proposed method, and Table II (p. 10) lists only SLP and computing parameters. The FL process (Algorithm 1, p. 6) is the application that the link serves: no FL model is trained or evaluated and no learning metric (accuracy, loss) is reported; Figs. 2-7 (pp. 11-13) show energy efficiency from the optimizer only. This is not FL over the air either: the uplink rate is a Shannon rate with FDMA bandwidth, Rk = bk log2(1+SINR) (p. 4, Eq. 5), or NOMA with SIC decoding (p. 10), so the aggregation is digital without over-the-air computation and would fall outside area 7 even if FL counted as the learned element. Other checks for the record: research article with simulation results (pp. 10-13), RIS-aided MIMO ISCC with Rician fading (p. 4), no standard channel model.
